answer: The willow multiplier is published, charged in wharf, and horizon lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3115 identities would post 1006 proofs and burn roughly 8 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
